newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: PRESS DIGEST - S.Korean newspapers - Nov 11.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - S.Korean newspapers - Nov 11.

text.p: The following is a summary of major South Korean political stories in leading newspapers, prepared by Reuters in Seoul. Reuters has not checked the stories and does not gaurantee their accuracy. Telephone: (822) 727-5650. Fax: (822) 727-5666.

- Labor law revision to be completed within the year. Major issues at stake between the government and labor unions include the abolition or revison of regulations restricting political activities, banning public servants and teachers from forming labor unions and banning outside intervention in labor disputes.
- The government to push for labour law revision before the year is over.
- Public charges have been main cause of inflation. Public charges rose by an average of 7.3 percent during the year.
- Labor law revision to be completed this year.
- Foundation of Paldang Bridge on the Han River is damaged and requires immediate repair. Despite being opened only one year ago, water has already eroded the base of the support column foundations.

- President Kim Young-sam repeated his opposition to talks with and aid to North Korea before the North apologises for recent submarine inclursions into South Korea, according to an exclusive Washington Post interview.
